item.title: The blue wave looks real until you look a little closer
item.description: The 2026 midterm elections are heating up as Republicans and Democrats battle for control of Congress. From Texas and Maine to Michigan, key Senate races, shifting polls and campaign spending battles add to the uncertainty, while both parties look ahead to the 2028 presidential race.
item.content:encoded:
It’s like watching some sci-fi game with players competing on 470 different fields. Which is your basic definition of crazytown. No human being, without mainlining AI into his or her arm, could possibly track so many contests, so we bounce from one race to the next, with buzzers and bells, like a pinball machine. 

Look! Charlie Cook is moving 18 House races in the Democrats’ favor! This is o-vah! The blue wave is getting stronger. Put a cork in this one, it’s done!

But wait a minute. The Republicans have a huge cash advantage. Big-time Democratic donors, for whatever reason, are sitting on their checkbooks. Don’t they realize the stakes? Are they all blinded by the sun on their private islands?

There seems to be a consensus, even privately among Republicans, that the Dems will take the House. The only question is the margin.

So we all wind-surf across the Senate race, even if we know little more than what we read that morning in Politico, or the New York Times or Wall Street Journal. 

The GOP just sent another $30 million to Ken Paxton, the Texas Republican who has more baggage than a 747. (Being impeached by your own party doesn’t help.) He was caught on audio saying "everybody’s numbers dropped" after President Trump’s midterm convention. Even Trump calls him "a pain in the *ss sometimes." And this is the guy they want to win?

DEMOCRATS THINK A BLUE WAVE IS BUILDING. HERE ARE 3 FORCES THAT COULD STOP IT

His Democratic opponent, James Talarico, went into hiding–what’s up with that? Turns out he had a nasty case of the flu. Still, it’s Texas, the Lone Star State, where Democratic dreams go to die.

Okay, we’re starting to get vertigo. In Maine, is this the year Susan Collins gets knocked off? One poll has her trailing by four points against Democrat Troy Jackson, who replaced weirdo candidate and Nazi tattoo-wearing Graham Platner, who quit after a sexual assault allegation. What a lovely business.

Republicans have a president who’s polling in the low 30s, which perhaps explains why he was campaigning the other day in Syracuse, when New York is among the bluest of blue states.

The Democrats need a net gain of four seats to control the Senate, and while some are prematurely sipping Champagne, nobody really knows if they can draw that kind of inside straight. If they tell you they do, they’re lying. 

MICHIGAN SENATE DEBATE ERUPTS INTO PERSONAL ATTACKS AS ROGERS, EL-SAYED CLASH OVER ISRAEL, IRAN AND MORE

There’s a harsh spotlight on the Michigan Senate race, featuring Democratic socialist Abdul el-Sayed vs. former congressman Mike Rogers. I eagerly watched their high-decibel debate the other night–okay, I was assigned to it--and here’s my takeaway.

El-Sayed won on points–he’s just a smoother and more aggressive debater than Rogers, who looks like a classic pol–and every third sentence was an attack on Trump or the war. This put Rogers at a disadvantage, because he supported the Iran war but now says it should end.

And El-Sayed kept whacking Rogers for owning two yachts, which is sort of irrelevant.

Rogers called his opponent a "con man" and kept trying to tie him to the Muslim Brotherhood. This was a weakness for el-Sayed, who was asked whether he’d send aid if Israel was attacked, and insisted that he’d rather spend the money here at home.

El-Sayed also did a lousy job of defending Medicare for All and why it wouldn’t bring the end of private insurance. Since Michigan is near the border, both men came out against Canadian tariffs–a flip for Rogers–in a noisy segment that was utterly indecipherable to mere mortals.

The whole thing turned into an interrup-ta-thon, with the moderator constantly scolding the contenders.

Aren’t you glad you missed it? Now, thanks to yours truly, you can pretend you saw the debate.

But enough about the midterms. Time to join the punditocracy and speculate about 2028.

Kamala Harris is leading the ridiculously early polls, with a quarter of the Democratic vote.

There’s just one problem. Her husband, the Wall Street Journal reports, has privately told people he doesn’t want her to run. How’s that for a vote of confidence?

So bite your nails, everyone. The fate of the free world, both sides are warning, hangs in the balance.

item.title: Suspect in deadly Philadelphia police ambush faces 76 charges, ordered held without bail
item.description: A Philadelphia man faces 76 charges, including murder, after allegedly ambushing police officers, killing one and wounding another, according to officials.
item.content:encoded:
The suspect accused in the ambush killing of a Philadelphia police officer was arraigned Sunday morning on 76 charges and ordered held without bail, according to court records.

Eric Lewis, 35, faces charges including murder, homicide of a law enforcement officer, attempted murder, 10 counts of attempted homicide of a law enforcement officer, aggravated assault, terroristic threats and other related offenses. His next court date is scheduled for Oct. 26.

The charges stem from a Saturday shooting that killed Philadelphia police Officer Shane Seiber and left his partner wounded.

Seiber, 40, was a father of two and an Air Force veteran who served 10 years with the Philadelphia Police Department. He is survived by his wife, 7-year-old son and 3-year-old daughter.

PHILADELPHIA POLICE OFFICER KILLED, PARTNER SHOT 12 TIMES IN AMBUSH; SUSPECT FOUND HIDING IN TREE

"He fought valiantly, but he lost his life today," Police Commissioner Kevin Bethel said at a news conference on Saturday. "His wife was able to be by his side before he passed, as well as his family."

The wounded officer, a 33-year-old father of five, was shot 12 times and was initially listed in critical condition. He has since been listed in stable condition.

The shooting unfolded around 12:20 a.m. Saturday, when the two officers responded to a report of a man with a gun. They located an armed man on a porch, according to police.

KENTUCKY TROOPER, FATHER OF 3, GUNNED DOWN DURING TRAFFIC STOP AS SUSPECT CAPTURED AFTER MANHUNT

The officers then came under "significant gunfire" after reaching the porch, police said.

Additional officers and a SWAT team arrived a short time later and found both officers on the porch suffering from gunshot wounds.

More gunfire followed, prompting authorities to declare a barricade situation before Lewis was eventually taken into custody, according to police.

Police said Lewis was found in possession of two handguns and a shotgun. One of the handguns belonged to an officer wounded in the attack.

At a news conference Saturday, District Attorney Larry Krasner declined to say whether Lewis had fired the officer's handgun or how he had obtained the other firearms.

Krasner also said there was nothing in Lewis' criminal background that would have prevented him from obtaining a firearm.

Lewis, an employee of the Philadelphia Water Department, has a criminal history dating to 2012, according to Pennsylvania court records reviewed by Fox News Digital.

Court records show Lewis was convicted of theft and receiving stolen property in 2012 and of gun-related offenses and simple assault in 2013. He received probation in both cases.

In 2018, Lewis pleaded guilty to disorderly conduct involving fighting and was again sentenced to probation.

Records also show Lewis received three traffic citations in 2024, including driving without headlights, failing to provide proof of insurance and a windshield-related violation.

Fox News' James Cirrone, Brittany Miller and CB Cotton contributed to this report.

item.title: Backup quarterback Tyler Huntley leads Baltimore Ravens to improbable OT win over Atlanta Falcons
item.description: Tyler Huntley scored three touchdowns to rally the Baltimore Ravens past the Atlanta Falcons 30-23 in a dramatic overtime Sunday Night Football win.
item.content:encoded:
You would have been forgiven if you had turned this game off sometime around the middle of the second quarter.

After all, both offenses were struggling to move the ball and the Baltimore Ravens were trotting out Tyler Huntley at quarterback in place of the injured Lamar Jackson.

However, just when it looked like this Sunday Night Football game was going to turn into a snoozer, the scoreboard decided to show a little life, as the Ravens came back to win 30-23 in overtime.

LAMAR JACKSON LEAVES GAME WITH INJURED ANKLE AND WHAT HAPPENED NEXT SHOWS NO ONE FEARS THE TENNESSEE TITANS

The Falcons took advantage of the aforementioned Huntley for much of the first half as the front seven specifically hounded the Ravens' offensive line to the tune of four sacks and numerous pressures.

When it counted though, Huntley made clutch play after clutch play with both his arms and his legs, showing both off on the game-tying final drive in regulation.

From there, a steady dose of Huntley and ageless wonder Derrick Henry would score the only touchdown of the extra frame.

Huntley's three touchdowns (two through the air and one on the ground) all came after the first half, when the Ravens couldn't muster much of anything to penetrate the Falcons' defense.

FALCONS' BIJAN ROBINSON BECOMES HIGHEST-PAID RUNNING BACK IN NFL HISTORY WITH MASSIVE CONTRACT: REPORT

On the other side of the field, Atlanta QB Michael Penix Jr. was opportunistic, converting on several third and longs in the second half to keep drives alive and effectively distributing the ball to his weapons.

As usual, Bijan Robinson had a nice night at the office, tallying over 100 yards from scrimmage, while wide receiver Drake London led the team with seven catches and 118 yards.

FALCONS STAR KYLE PITTS SR PREDICTS CFB PLAYERS WILL UNIONIZE, SAYS PRO PLAYERS RETURNING TO SCHOOL IS 'CRAZY'

Even Kyle Pitts got in on the fun and looked closer to his 2025 All-Pro form, reeling in five receptions for 42 yards including an eight-yard score in the first half.

When the Falcons' "big three" are all having productive games, this offense can be hard to stop.

In the end, though, their efforts were ultimately in vain.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Penix was unable to finish the game after taking a shot to the ribs late in the fourth quarter.

Backup Tua Tagovailoa came on in relief for one play before taking over permanently in overtime.

After a promising start to the potential game-tying drive in the extra frame, Tagovailoa would toss an interception to Baltimore All-Pro safety Kyle Hamilton to seal Atlanta's fate.

The Ravens needed this win, as the victory pushes them to 4-1 and nets them sole possession of first place in the AFC North.

Meanwhile, the Falcons will fall to 2-3, and head coach Kevin Stefanski will be left wondering how he let this opportunity slip through his hands.

item.title: Pope Leo denounces death penalty as 'inadmissible' ahead of Pentagon's planned livestreamed execution
item.description: Pope Leo XIV called the death penalty "inadmissible" on World Day Against the Death Penalty after the Pentagon announced plans to livestream an execution.
item.content:encoded:
Pope Leo XIV condemned the death penalty as "inadmissible" as the Pentagon faces criticism over plans to livestream an execution later this year.

Leo, the first American pope, shared his opposition to capital punishment Saturday in a social media post marking World Day Against the Death Penalty.

Citing Catholic doctrine revised under his predecessor, Pope Francis, Leo emphasized that the death penalty violates human dignity.

"The death penalty is inadmissible because it is an attack on the inviolability and dignity of the person. The common good can be safeguarded and the requirements of justice can be met without recourse to capital punishment: effective systems of detention have been developed that protect citizens while at the same time do not completely deprive those who are guilty of the possibility of redemption," Leo wrote on X.

"#NoDeathPenalty," he added in the post.

VETERAN SHOT 7 TIMES IN FORT HOOD MASSACRE HAS A WARNING FOR AMERICANS PLANNING TO WATCH EXECUTION

In 2018, Francis revised the Catholic Church's official position on capital punishment, declaring the death penalty "inadmissible" in all circumstances.

"Consequently the church teaches, in the light of the Gospel, that the death penalty is inadmissible because it is an attack on the inviolability and dignity of the person," the revised Catechism states.

Before the change, Catholic teaching permitted the death penalty in cases where it was deemed the only effective means of protecting human life from a dangerous offender.

Earlier popes had maintained that exception, though Pope John Paul II increasingly advocated ending capital punishment, stressing that those convicted of crimes retain their human dignity.

Although Leo did not specifically mention the U.S. government's plans in his statement, his post comes after the Pentagon announced on Thursday that it had scheduled a firing squad execution for a man convicted of a mass shooting at a military base.

Nidal Malik Hasan, a former Army psychiatrist, was convicted of killing 13 people and wounding 32 others in a 2009 shooting at the Fort Hood military base. He is set to be executed at Fort Hood on Dec. 3, which would make him the first person to be executed by firing squad by the U.S. military since 1945.

President Donald Trump said on Saturday he had not yet decided whether to allow the livestream plan, pushed by Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth, to move forward.

Vice President JD Vance, who is a Catholic, expressed skepticism about whether the Pentagon would proceed with a public execution. He said he would not watch the livestream if it were carried out.

Several lawmakers, including Republicans, have spoken out against plans to broadcast the execution.

CHRISTA PIKE DISCHARGED FROM HOSPITAL, RETURNED TO PRISON AFTER BOTCHED EXECUTION, ATTORNEYS SAY

"Public executions are what oppressive dictatorships like Iran and Afghanistan do," Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., said on Thursday. "It should not be happening in America."

Cardinal Pietro Parolin, the Vatican secretary of state, criticized the proposed broadcast, calling it "truly incomprehensible" and warning that it was "unacceptable to turn death into a spectacle."

"The Church’s position is one of total opposition to the death penalty; it is incompatible with human dignity and serves as no deterrent," Parolin told reporters on Friday. "It is truly incomprehensible that anyone would want to use this system today — I don’t know for what purpose. It is certainly unacceptable to turn death into a spectacle; even if the person is guilty, of course, there are other methods."

He added that the death penalty "is incompatible with human dignity and does not serve as a deterrent."

The head of the U.S. bishops conference, Archbishop Paul Coakley, expressed "shock" and "great sorrow" about the public execution plan and urged the U.S. to reconsider.

"In no way can Hasan’s actions be condoned but this decision is a barbaric promotion of a culture of death and must be reconsidered," he said in a statement on Friday. "The public execution even of one who has done grave harm will only further undermine the moral fabric of our nation and be a blight on the conscience of its people."

Leo's statement also did not mention the botched lethal injection of Christa Gail Pike in Tennessee. Pike survived the attempted execution despite two doses of pentobarbital being administered late last month.

The Associated Press and Reuters contributed to this report.

item.title: Brewers stun Dodgers, 2-1, in NLCS Game 1 as LA's offense flops with runners in scoring position
item.description: Even MLB's powerhouse Dodgers couldn't solve the Milwaukee Brewers in NLCS Game 1 as Jacob Misiorowski struck out five in a dominant home stand.
item.content:encoded:
Even MLB's powerhouse team needs a wake-up call. And this time around in the NLCS, the Milwaukee Brewers eked out a statement win versus the boys in blue.

The Brewers defended home turf in Game 1 of the NLCS, defeating the Los Angeles Dodgers 2–1 in a tight pitching duel. After getting swept by the Dodgers in last year's NLCS, Milwaukee hopes to rewrite the script and capitalize on their regular-season-best record.

Milwaukee flamethrower Jacob Misiorowski pitched 4 1/3 innings, allowing five hits, one run, and three walks while striking out five. He threw 94 pitches (60 strikes).

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Baseball's unicorn, Shohei Ohtani, continued his postseason struggles, and LA newcomer Tarik Skubal had a forgettable outing on the mound as Pat Murphy's "underdog" Brewers edged the back-to-back champs.

LA scored first in the second inning, bringing in Ohtani with an Andy Pages RBI single to right. Milwaukee responded in the bottom of the fourth with a Brice Turang solo homer. The Brewers inserted 21-year-old Luis Lara in a big spot, and he delivered in the fifth with an RBI single to score Garrett Mitchell for the go-ahead run.

Skubal tallied 81 pitches through five innings, prompting LA manager Dave Roberts to activate the bullpen earlier than expected. Skubal gave up five hits and two runs while recording seven strikeouts.

The Dodgers will turn to generational ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto in Game 2, though LA rarely puts on an offensive showcase when Yoshi is on the bump.

LA struggled to bring in runners, an issue that has plagued prime NL contenders in recent memory, like last year's Brewers and 2024's NLCS Mets. The Dodgers went 1-for-5 with runners in scoring position and left eight on base. With a final chance to tie in the ninth, LA put the tying run in scoring position after Trevor Megill issued two-out walks to Kyle Tucker and pinch-hitter Josue De Paula, but Megill induced a game-ending flyout from Mookie Betts to preserve the huge win.

The Dodgers left nine guys on base Sunday night.

Historically, teams that win Game 1 of a League Championship Series advance 65.6% of the time; home teams winning Game 1 hold a 67.3% win rate.

item.title: Maduro-linked fugitive nabbed over alleged scheme to cash in on Venezuelans’ basic needs
item.description: Alvaro Pulido Vargas allegedly exploited Venezuela's CLAP food program and housing contracts, funneling billions through U.S. banks to hide bribes.
item.content:encoded:
A fugitive accused of getting rich off programs meant to help Venezuelans is now in U.S. custody, facing charges in a sprawling corruption scandal tied to Nicolás Maduro’s regime.

Alvaro Pulido Vargas, 62, was arrested during a Homeland Security Task Force operation and is scheduled to appear Tuesday, Oct. 13, in federal court in South Florida, the Justice Department announced.

The Colombian national faces two criminal cases alleging he helped funnel money from Venezuelan government bribery schemes through U.S. banks to hide illicit profits.

NICOLAS MADURO AND WIFE CILIA FLORES FACE NEW CHARGE OF CONSPIRACY TO TORTURE AMERICANS

"Pulido is charged in two separate, significant money laundering schemes, both using the U.S. financial system to hide the profits from his bribery and greed off the backs of the Venezuelan people," said Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva.

Attorney General Todd Blanche announced the arrest Sunday on X, accusing Pulido Vargas of exploiting programs meant to provide essential supplies and housing.

"His alleged actions show a blatant disregard to the Venezuelan people by corrupting government programs intended to provide critical food, medicine, and housing for personal enrichment and exploiting the American financial system to do it," Blanche wrote.

Pulido Vargas, also known as German Enrique Rubio Salas, was charged in 2019 and again in 2021. The Justice Department said he previously was convicted of drug trafficking in Italy in 1997 under that alias.

"For years, DEA and our HSTF partners have pursued Pulido Vargas across borders. Today, that pursuit has brought him to the Southern District of Florida," DEA Administrator Terrance Cole said.

The newer case centers on approximately $1.6 billion in Venezuelan government contracts to supply food and medicine through CLAP, a government-run distribution program.

OUR ADVERSARIES ARE EVEN USING THE US BANKING SYSTEM. HERE’S HOW THEY GET AWAY WITH IT

Prosecutors say Pulido Vargas and his associates paid bribes to win the contracts, then inflated prices to cover the payoffs and line their own pockets. The alleged scheme ran from approximately July 2015 through at least 2020.

His son, Emmanuel Enrique Rubio Gonzalez, and former Venezuelan state governor Jose Gregorio Vielma-Mora were among four others charged in the case.

NICOLÁS MADURO AND HIS WIFE EXPECTED TO FACE NEW CHARGES RELATED TO ALLEGED TORTURE OF AMERICANS

Prosecutors say Vielma-Mora and a middleman collected roughly $17.3 million in bribes and illicit payments for helping steer government food contracts and other business advantages to the group.

The money allegedly flowed through a web of companies and bank accounts in Antigua, the United Arab Emirates, the United States and elsewhere. The 2021 indictment describes fake contracts and other paperwork allegedly used to make the payments appear legitimate.

Approximately $180 million moved through or into the United States, including accounts in South Florida, according to prosecutors.

"The allegations describe a profound betrayal of the Venezuelan people; corrupting government programs intended to provide critical food, medicine, and housing for personal enrichment," said U.S. Attorney Jason A. Reding Quiñones.

MADURO CLAIMS IMMUNITY, ASKS JUDGE TO DISMISS DRUG-TRAFFICKING CHARGES AGAINST HIM AND HIS WIFE

The earlier case centers on an alleged scheme to cash in on a government program meant to build homes for low-income Venezuelans.

Prosecutors charged Pulido Vargas and Maduro ally Alex Nain Saab Moran in 2019, accusing them of using a housing contract to exploit Venezuela’s government-controlled currency exchange system.

NICOLÁS MADURO FLASHES PEACE SIGNS IN FIRST PRISON PHOTOS SINCE US CAPTURE IN CARACAS

The men allegedly submitted false paperwork claiming they had imported goods and building materials that never entered Venezuela, then bribed officials to approve those documents.

Prosecutors say they moved approximately $350 million out of Venezuela through U.S. banks and into overseas accounts they controlled. The alleged scheme ran from approximately November 2011 through at least September 2015.

Pulido Vargas faces five money laundering-related charges in the 2021 case, each carrying a maximum sentence of 20 years in federal prison. He faces eight additional money laundering-related charges in the 2019 case.

The DEA, FBI and Homeland Security Investigations are investigating the cases through the Homeland Security Task Force initiative.

Blanche pointed to the arrest as a warning to others facing U.S. prosecution.

"No amount of time or distance will stop @TheJusticeDept from working with our federal law enforcement and international partners to pursue these criminals and bring them to justice in an American courtroom," he wrote.

item.title: At least 139 migrants dead, 84 missing after overcrowded boat capsizes off Djibouti
item.description: More than 80 people survived the deadly crossing from Djibouti toward Yemen, while at least 84 remained missing as authorities worked to verify additional victims.
item.content:encoded:
At least 139 migrants, including 15 children, died when a boat carrying more than 300 people capsized off the coast of Djibouti, according to the United Nations' migration agency.

The vessel was carrying 305 people from Djibouti toward Yemen when it capsized Thursday night or early Friday near Guhere, north of Obock, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) said Sunday.

At least 84 people remained missing as of Sunday, while more than 80 survived. All of the survivors were Ethiopian nationals, according to the agency.

"No one gets into a boat like that unless they believe there is no other safe way," IOM Director General Amy Pope said in a statement. 

DRAMATIC FOOTAGE SHOWS ALLEGED NARCO BOAT ERUPT IN FIREBALL DURING US MILITARY STRIKE

"We cannot keep treating these deaths as normal. Safe and legal pathways save lives. I am asking governments and donors to act before the next boat goes down," Pope added.

The confirmed death toll includes only victims buried by authorities in Djibouti and could rise as additional bodies are verified, IOM Chief of Mission in Djibouti Alexandre Coissac told The Associated Press.

Some victims were buried by fellow migrants but will not be added to the official count until authorities can verify the bodies, the outlet reported.

BOATER WAS DRUNK, DANCING BEFORE BOSTON HARBOR CRASH THAT KILLED 24-YEAR-OLD FORMER SOCCER PLAYER, DA SAYS

"What is terrible is that they were buried with no names, in a common grave, like in a war situation," Coissac said. "They all have a mother, a father, and we may never learn what happened."

Coissac said the boat sank shortly after departing on the evening of Oct. 8, "mainly because it was overcrowded."

Survivors were taken to an IOM rescue center in Obock, where they were receiving medical treatment after swallowing seawater as well as psychological support, according to The Associated Press.

FEDERAL AGENTS INTERCEPT BOAT CARRYING 14 ILLEGAL ALIENS BEFORE UNLOADING IN WEALTHY COASTAL ENCLAVE

"They're all in a state of shock," Coissac said.

The crossing from the Horn of Africa to the Arabian Peninsula is a common but dangerous route for migrants seeking work in Gulf countries.

More than 900 migrants died or went missing along the route last year, according to the IOM.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Houthis kill 14 at Saudi airport as expert warns of 'rapid targets' amid Middle East war
item.description: Iran-backed Houthis struck Saudi Arabian airports in Riyadh and Dammam, killing at least 14 and injuring over 300 as experts warn of wider war.
item.content:encoded:
Iran-backed Houthis launched a series of attacks on Saudi Arabian airports through Sunday, reportedly killing at least 14 people, including an American, and injuring more than 300 others, according to reports.

The attacks heightened fears of a wider Middle East war as regional experts warned of "cross-domain escalation" amid heightened tensions over Washington's September actions against Iran's aviation sector.

The Houthis claimed responsibility for earlier attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, while U.S. officials blamed the Iran-backed group for Saturday's strike, which reportedly killed 13 people and injured more than 300.

SAUDI FOREIGN MINISTER WARNS HOUTHI THREAT GOES GLOBAL AS TRUMP HOLDS FIRE

Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said another attack on Sunday killed a Pakistani resident and injured 11 others. Meanwhile, an airport in Dammam, in the kingdom's Eastern Province, was also reportedly targeted by the Houthis.

"Cross-domain escalation by Iran and its proxies will continue to be a primary strategy," Behnam Ben Taleblu, senior director of the Iran Program and a senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies, told Fox News Digital on Sunday.

"The emphasis on aviation targets connects directly to the closing of Iran's aviation sector and sanctions imposed on its commercial airlines under the U.S. maximum pressure campaign," he warned.

RUBIO ACCUSES IRAN OF FLYING IRGC PERSONNEL INTO YEMEN AS HOUTHI THREAT ESCALATES

The Houthis also renewed warnings Sunday, urging airlines, airport workers and travelers to avoid Saudi airports as Saudi Arabia vowed to retaliate for the deadly attacks.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio condemned Saturday's attack, confirming that an American was among those killed and calling for an immediate end to the violence.

President Donald Trump, meanwhile, left open the possibility of U.S. involvement in Saudi Arabia's military campaign against the Houthis, saying, "We may. We're gonna look at it. We move very quickly."

The escalation comes nearly three weeks after a senior Iranian official threatened to paralyze neighboring countries' airports if they cooperated with U.S. efforts to restrict Iranian flights.

THE HOUTHIS AREN'T SOMEBODY ELSE'S PROBLEM. AMERICA CAN'T AFFORD TO LOOK AWAY

Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, warned Sept. 23 that Iran would prevent neighboring countries' airports from operating if they cooperated with Washington's efforts to restrict Iranian flights, according to Reuters.

"This rapid targeting reflects earlier threats made by Iranian officials, including a veiled threat from the Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, warning that U.S. sanctions on Iran's aviation sector would lead to retaliatory threats against neighboring aviation infrastructure," Taleblu said.

Iran has long supported the Houthis, but the extent of Tehran's involvement in the latest airport attacks has not been independently established.

The escalation has also renewed scrutiny of reports that Russia has provided intelligence and technical assistance to the Houthis.

FOILED TERROR PLOT AT BOMBER BASE SIGNALS WIDER THREAT TO US MILITARY INSTALLATIONS: EXPERT

At a Sept. 1 House Foreign Affairs subcommittee hearing , lawmakers pressed experts on allegations that Russia is providing intelligence and technical support to the Houthis.

"Beyond offering diplomatic cover, there are persistent reports of Russian satellite collaboration, advisory support, and intelligence targeting assistance, as well as unproven allegations regarding select anti-ship systems."

HOUTHIS ENTER US 'KILL BOX' AFTER SEIZING RED SEA 'CORK,' FORMER PENTAGON OFFICIAL WARNS

But he also linked the latest attacks to a broader military escalation as the Houthis expand their territorial control in Yemen.

"This surge did not occur in a vacuum," Taleblu said. "Since April, the Houthis have made territorial gains and pushed back against Saudi forces despite a period of diplomatic lull."

"Airport attacks allow Iran and its regional proxies to inflict pain on Arab states, Israel, and remaining U.S. forces," Taleblu said.

item.title: Ella Langley says canceled concert was ‘not worth a human life’ after bomb threat
item.description: Ella Langley became emotional during her Texas concert explaining why she canceled her sold-out BOK Center show despite Tulsa police finding no credible threat.
item.content:encoded:
Ella Langley is speaking out about her decision to cancel her concert in Tulsa, Oklahoma, following a reported bomb threat.

The 27-year-old country star addressed the cancellation while performing in Lubbock, Texas, one day after calling off her sold-out Friday night show at Tulsa's BOK Center.

Langley became emotional while explaining why she decided not to perform despite police finding no credible threat.

MEGAN MORONEY CANCELS SHOW MID-PERFORMANCE, LEAVES STAGE IN TEARS

"I was put in charge of a decision for 15,000 people and I decided to make the decision that I could live with the rest of my life," the "Choosin' Texas" hitmaker told the crowd on Saturday night at the United Supermarkets Arena, according to Taste of Country.

"Because when it comes to keeping you safe and making sure that this show is a safe place for us to come and enjoy our music, then it will happen," she continued. "But the second, it feels like it's not, I'm not doing it. I'm not doing it because a concert's not worth a human life. It's not."

ED SHEERAN APOLOGIZES FOR MACKLEMORE BACKLASH, ENCOURAGES UNITY AT FIRST CONCERT SINCE FALLOUT

"And so I would have made yesterday's decision ten billion times over," she added. "And I'd do it tomorrow and I'd do it the next day."

Langley went on to explain that the safety of her fans outweighed her desire to perform.

"Because while I'm grateful to get to do what I do, it's not the most important thing in this life," she said. "What's the most important thing in this life is the people around you that love you and that are there for you no matter what."

"The most important thing in this life is that you wake up every day and feel like, 'You know what, I'm good today. I am so grateful to have woken up today,'" Langley continued.

ELLA LANGLEY DELIVERS POWERFUL FAITH MESSAGE TO CROWD DURING MORGAN WALLEN CONCERT IN CHICAGO

"The most important thing in this life, number one, is your relationship with Jesus Christ," she added.

Langley admitted that she nearly canceled Saturday's concert in Texas because she was still shaken by the incident. However, she credited her faith in Jesus with giving her the courage to return to the stage.

ELLA LANGLEY GOES VIRAL WITH PASSIONATE COMMENTS ABOUT HER CHRISTIAN FAITH, GOD, LOVE AND RELIGION

"If it wasn't for Him," I would have canceled this show tonight," she told the crowd. "I would have."

"But I felt this calling and this tug in my chest saying, 'It's OK. We are safe. We can do this show,'" Langley continued. "And I decided to do it because of Him right there. And that's the only reason."

ELLA LANGLEY'S FAITH AND AUTHENTICITY FUEL RECORD-BREAKING RISE, EXPERTS SAY

"I'm not gonna live in fear," Langley added. "We're going to put on music and get to do this for the rest of our lives. And I know that. I know because this is my calling. This is the thing that I was called to do, and I'm going to continue doing it. Nobody is going to take me out of it or scare me out."

Langley expressed her gratitude to her fans for coming to her Texas show despite the frightening incident at the Oklahoma concert.

"I know yesterday was scary, it was scary for all of us," she said. "But we're just so grateful to be playing this show tonight. We're so grateful and we will never take this for granted. We love it, we love what we do. I wouldn't trade it for the world."

"Tonight I can tell that y'all knew that I've needed what you've given me. And this band and this crew — you knew that we needed this show tonight, so thank you so much for giving it to us," Langley added.

ED SHEERAN'S GILLETTE STADIUM CONCERTS CALLED OFF AS TROUBLED TOUR FACES FRESH SETBACK

Langley announced the cancelation of Friday night's concert on Instagram approximately two hours before the show was scheduled to begin.

"Due to a serious security threat involving the safety of my fans, the venue staff, and my team, the incredibly difficult decision was made to cancel tonight’s show. This decision was made under the advisement of local authorities, the venue, and my security team," the singer began.

She said the decision followed guidance from local authorities, venue officials and her security team, adding that she refused to put anyone in danger.

"I know how much time, travel, money, and planning goes into coming to a show, and I can’t tell you how sorry I am. This is not a decision that was made lightly. I was so looking forward to spending tonight with you, but your safety will always mean more to me than anything else. I refuse to put anyone in harm’s way," the country music star's statement concluded.

The BOK Center also released a statement on Friday. "The safety and well-being of everyone involved is our absolute priority, and after careful consideration, we have determined that the show cannot proceed. We understand the disappointment this news brings and apologize to fans who planned to attend. The safety of fans is our foremost concern and will always come first," the statement read.

The official Instagram account for the BOK Center said that ticket refunds and additional information will be shared as soon as possible.

Langley's explanation for her decision to cancel the concert comes after the Tulsa Police Department said that they found no credible threat to the event.

In a since-deleted statement posted to Facebook, the department explained that officers had conducted routine security sweeps before the concert using K-9 units, bomb technicians, patrol officers and venue security personnel and "did not find anything" dangerous.

"A call was made threatening the lives of people attending the event," they continued. "Out of an abundance of caution, we swept the building and surrounding area and again found no credible threat to the event's safety. We advised the performer's staff that we found no credible threat to the event, but they decided to cancel the performance anyway."

Tulsa Police Department Capt. Richard Meulenberg provided additional details in a video posted to Facebook that has since been deleted. Meulenberg said that after the first security sweeps, "the event was ready to go," according to Saving Country Music.

"And then what happened was a call came in, saying that someone was going to [do] great harm to the people here at this event in the way of shots fired and bombs. So we came out again in an overabundance of caution, used our bomb dogs again, searched the entire area, we could not find a credible threat here at the BOK Center," he said. "We apologize to everyone who came down to the Tulsa area for this. But everything is safe."

In an interview with Tulsa news station Fox23, Meulenberg also emphasized that the department did not recommend canceling the concert.

We could not find anything that would make that a credible threat. We advised the group here that was supposed to perform that we could not find a credible threat. A spokesperson later told "Good Morning America" that the incident remains under investigation, with the FBI assisting.

item.title: Tom Emmer tells Jon Karl there are 'communists' on the midterm ballot in heated ABC exchange
item.description: House Majority Whip Tom Emmer clashed with Jon Karl on ABC's "This Week," insisting that Democratic socialists on the ballot are actually communists.
item.content:encoded:
House Majority Whip Tom Emmer, R-Minn., pushed back against ABC's "This Week" host Jon Karl after he insisted "there aren’t a lot of communists on the ballot" Sunday.

The clash began after Emmer conceded the Republican Party needed to make an effort to lower gas prices ahead of the midterm elections.

"I would say this on that, $4 gas, $6 diesel, entirely unacceptable," Emmer said. "We Republicans agree on that. But it’s not enough to vote for communists."

"I think most Democrats would say they’re not communists," Karl replied with a chuckle. "So, there aren’t a lot of communists on the ballot in these midterms."

SHOCKING PERCENTAGE OF DEMOCRATS IDENTIFY AS 'DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS' ACCORDING TO NEW POLL: 'TOXIC POLICIES'

"Well you’re wrong, they are communists," Emmer interrupted.

Karl conceded that there were "some Democratic socialists" on the ballot and attempted to move on to a new topic, but Emmer rejected the idea.

"Jon, you just called them what they want you to call them. There’s nothing Democratic about socialism. For 100 years, they wanted us to call them progressives, when, in fact, they were socialists. And it wasn’t cool to admit you’re a socialist. They are now communists and Marxists. Take a look at the [Democratic Socialists of America] platform," Emmer said.

Karl again attempted to change topics, but Emmer continued.

VULNERABLE DEMOCRAT WARNS PARTY TO 'FIGHT BACK' AGAINST GROWING SOCIALIST MOVEMENT

"They want to defund the police. They want to defund prisons. They want government-only health care. And they want the Green New Deal, which will cost every American family another $355,000. That’s what we should be talking about," Emmer said.

Earlier in the interview, Emmer also criticized mainstream media for framing inflation and high gas prices under President Donald Trump differently from how they reported them under former President Joe Biden.

"I hate to point the finger at you and the other journalists, but have you reported that under Joe Biden, the average was over $5 a gallon? Under Donald Trump, he’s pulled it all the way back, even with the action that had to be taken to make sure that Iran never has a nuclear weapon. It’s closer to $4. It’s about 13 percent below what Joe Biden had. Grocery inflation. Under Biden, it was 13-point-something. Under Donald Trump, it’s two percent. It’s 11 points better. But you guys don’t report this stuff. So, I’m not saying the American people don’t get it. They don’t get the truth from the people that are reporting it," Emmer said.

MORE AMERICANS THAN EVER NOW HAVE A POSITIVE VIEW OF SOCIALISM, NEW POLL SAYS

Fox News Digital reached out to Emmer and ABC News for comment.

Emmer made similar comments in an interview with Fox News Digital last week when he accused the far-left wing of the Democratic Party of being "communists, Marxists and anarchists." He especially took issue with Democratic Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, though he has denied being a socialist.

"This guy says ridiculous things like U.S. NFL football is an example of toxic masculinity, he supports a terrorist who believes that America deserved to lose 3,000 people on 9/11, and he's got this Piker guy who's just shooting his mouth off on everything anti-American," Emmer said. "These people are anti-American more than anything else." 

Emmer's comments come as dozens of Democratic Socialists of America-backed candidates run for office during the midterm elections.

item.title: Should Penn State already regret James Franklin firing after loss to USC in 'White Out' game?
item.description: USC-Penn State drew a record 114,419 fans for Beaver Stadium's 'White Out,' but Jayden Maiava's three touchdowns silenced the crowd in a huge road win.
item.content:encoded:
Lost among the other big games of week six of the college football season, Oklahoma-Texas, UCLA-Oregon, and Georgia-Alabama, was the most highly attended game of them all: USC-Penn State.

Despite the 2026 season being disappointing, to varying degrees, for both schools, it was still a highly anticipated matchup of two big programs looking to salvage their year. Penn State chose to make it the "White Out" game, then sold an incredible number of tickets. A record-breaking number, in fact.

The Nittany Lions announced the highest attendance in Beaver Stadium history, packing in a remarkable 114,419 fans for the 7:30 p.m. EDT kickoff. Penn State was coming off a brutal 34-13 loss to Northwestern where they allowed a whopping 506 total yards, including an almost incomprehensible 413 rushing yards to the Wildcat ground game. USC was one week removed from an ugly 25-21 win over Washington, and two weeks removed from a very poor 41-27 loss to Oregon.

FIVE IMPORTANT COLLEGE FOOTBALL QUESTIONS THAT WILL BE ANSWERED AFTER THIS WEEKEND'S SLATE

For Lincoln Riley, this had become the latest "must-win" game. Already on the hot seat, despite his massive buyout, a loss would effectively end any chance USC had of reaching the College Football Playoff thanks to upcoming games against Ohio State and Indiana. Under Riley, SC has also struggled mightily on the road, particularly in the Eastern Time Zone. Entering Saturday, the Trojans had gone just 4-7 in away games since joining the Big Ten.

For Penn State, despite the ugly loss to Northwestern, it was a chance to make several statements. One, that Beaver Stadium is still one of the toughest places to play in the country, and two, that the Nittany Lions would progress in year one of the Matt Campbell era by winning "big games" against ranked teams.

Instead, SC made the statement, and in the process, may have cooled off Riley's seat just a bit.

Jayden Maiava played one of the best games of his career, completing 21 of 33 passing attempts with three touchdowns, controlling the offense while the running backs struggled to get going. In the second half, as the Nittany Lions defense wore down, King Miller and Waymond Jordan took over, including salting away the game on the final drive in the fourth quarter. Trent Mosley, who'd missed the last couple of games with an injury, showed why he's arguably the most electric freshman in the country, catching nine passes for 111 yards and a touchdown.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Penn State, meanwhile, just wasn't good enough. Against the typically mediocre USC defense, their running attack was virtually non-existent with just 68 yards on 31 attempts. On several second-half drives, the Nittany Lions couldn't get into the end zone after long drives, settling for disappointing field goals.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

After USC took an eight-point lead in the fourth quarter, they had a first and 10 at the USC 39-yard line with 6:31 to go. They went incomplete pass, incomplete pass, sack, punt. Even after forcing a punt and getting the ball back, Penn State immediately fumbled the ball right back to the Trojans.

SC ran out the clock thanks to a few first downs and another inexplicable PSU mistake. On 3rd-and-3 with just over a minute remaining, the Penn State d-line was called for delay of game for using signals to try and force SC into a false start. Automatic first down, game over. And it came after Riley got Campbell to burn his final timeout by using an unorthodox punt formation.

Lincoln Riley outcoaching someone else? Stop the presses.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

The Trojans, and Riley, had to win this game. Penn State is clearly in a rebuilding year after losing many of their players with the James Franklin firing. Their upcoming schedule is brutal; a road game against a suddenly-improved Wisconsin, Ohio State in LA, another road game at Indiana, before closing the season at the Rose Bowl against an impressive UCLA team.

Finish 10-2 and there's a chance for the College Football Playoff. But a loss to Penn State might have sent the season off the rails, heading for a 7-5 or 8-4 record that could get Riley fired. That's still a possibility, of course, but overcoming the largest crowd in Penn State history was a necessary first step. Can SC take the next few, arguably tougher steps? It's unlikely, yes, but still possible.

Penn State fans and boosters though, might already be regretting their program's big reset. The end of Franklin's tenure in Happy Valley was disappointing, to say the least, but the Nittany Lions were just a few plays away from competing for a National Championship in the 2024-2025 College Football Playoff. Now they've lost three games in a row and are coming off back-to-back poor performances defensively in which they've allowed 936 total yards to Northwestern and USC.

The schedule gets easier from here on out, but this is hardly the type of progress fans were hoping for in year one of the Matt Campbell era. It's one thing to lose to elite Ohio State or Michigan teams, it's another to lose three games before the middle of October. James Franklin may not have been the coach to win Penn State a national title, but thus far, there hasn't been much to suggest they're closer to that goal now than they were a year ago.

USC has a bye before going to Wisconsin, while Penn State has to immediately regroup for a road trip to Michigan. Seems like both those games will tell us a lot about the direction these programs are heading in.

item.title: Pregnant mom just 4 days from giving birth among 8 killed in Pennsylvania massacre: reports
item.description: Angelina Stone, who was eight months pregnant, was killed along with her two young children and several relatives in a mass shooting at a home in Erie, Pennsylvania, according to reports.
item.content:encoded:
A pregnant Pennsylvania woman who was reportedly just four days away from giving birth and her two young children were among eight victims killed in a mass shooting at an Erie home Friday.

Angelina Stone, who was eight months pregnant, was killed along with her children and several other relatives, according to local reports. 

CBS Pittsburgh reported that Stone was four days away from giving birth, while a family friend told Erie News Now she was expected to deliver "in a couple of days."

A GoFundMe organized to help with funeral expenses identified Stone's children as Isiah and Amari’anna and her unborn baby as Kyrie.

MONTANA MAN WHO KILLED 4 CHILDREN, 4 OTHER FAMILY MEMBERS AT SUNDAY DINNER WAS ASKED TO MOVE OUT: RELATIVE

"This situation is horrific and unimaginable," neighbor Jennifer Macko told CBS Pittsburgh.

Lisa Simmers, a family friend, remembered Stone's children as "beautiful, beautiful children" who "definitely did not deserve what happened to them."

"She had a daughter that was almost two, and her son Isiah, who I believe was like four or five," Simmers told Erie News Now.

Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah said Saturday that eight victims were killed in the Friday evening shooting before the suspected gunman, a 45-year-old man, died from what investigators believe was a self-inflicted gunshot wound.

8 FAMILY MEMBERS, INCLUDING 6 CHILDREN, FOUND DEAD IN MICHIGAN FIRE; AT LEAST ONE VICTIM SHOT: POLICE

The suspected gunman was related to seven of the eight victims and was the family's patriarch and a grandfather, according to police and a relative who spoke to The Associated Press. The eighth victim was a family friend, Lorah said.

Police Chief Rick Lorah said mental health may have played a role in the shooting but cautioned that it was too early to determine a motive..

Investigators believe all eight victims and the suspected gunman died before officers arrived.

The GoFundMe organizer said the family was seeking help covering funeral expenses for Stone and her children.

"I'm raising funds for Angelina, Isiah, baby girl Amari’anna, and unborn Kyrie after an unthinkable tragedy," the fundraiser states.

TWO TEEN SUSPECTS HELD AFTER 5 FAMILY MEMBERS KILLED IN 'TARGETED MASS SHOOTING'

The organizer added, "This is more than our family can carry alone right now, and we truly need the community to rally around us. Any donation, no matter the amount, will help ease the financial burden and help us give Angelina, Isiah, Amari’anna, and Kyrie the farewell they deserve."

The Erie Police Department continues to investigate.

The Erie Police Department could not immediately be reached by Fox News Digital for comment.

Fox News Digital's Michael Sinkewicz, Robert McGreevy and Brittany Miller contributed to this report.

item.title: Minnesota homecoming shooting suspect out on bond after gunfire sends football fans fleeing
item.description: Adam Abdihakeem Adam posted bond two days after his arrest in the Eden Prairie homecoming shooting, drawing sharp criticism from President Donald Trump's team.
item.content:encoded:
A Minnesota homecoming celebration shattered by gunfire has become the latest flashpoint over crime and bail after the accused shooter was released from jail just two days after his arrest.

Adam Abdihakeem Adam, 18, posted bond and was released Saturday evening, according to Hennepin County jail records reviewed by Fox News Digital.

Police say he shot two teenagers outside Eden Prairie High School during its Oct. 2 homecoming football game, prompting the evacuation of the stadium.

His release drew criticism from President Donald Trump’s Rapid Response 47 account, which highlighted police statements linking the shooting to rival Somali gangs.

POLICE MAKE ARREST AFTER GUNFIRE DURING CALIFORNIA HIGH SCHOOL FOOTBALL GAME LEAVES 1 DEAD

"A Radical Left judge immediately granted him a no-condition bail," the account wrote on X.

Jail records list a $100,000 bail or bond option without conditions and show Adam was released at 7:04 p.m. Oct. 10. He faces two felony counts of second-degree assault with a dangerous weapon and one count of second-degree riot while armed with a dangerous weapon. His next court appearance is scheduled for Monday afternoon.

MARYLAND MAN ACCUSED OF GIRL'S FATAL SHOOTING RELEASED FROM PRISON DAYS BEFORE

The shooting injured an 18-year-old and a 17-year-old and launched a multi-agency hunt for those involved, according to Eden Prairie police.

Investigators allege the violence began after two cars entered a parking lot and a fight involving about 10 people broke out. The driver of one car got out, opened fire on the victims and fled, according to charging documents cited by affiliate FOX 9 Minneapolis.

Authorities identified that driver as Adam, who allegedly was driving his brother’s car. Investigators tracked his phone with the vehicle before, during and after the shooting, the outlet reported. He then allegedly abandoned the phone and changed his number.

SHOOTING NEAR BALTIMORE YOUTH FOOTBALL EVENT LEAVES 12-YEAR-OLD GIRL DEAD, 3 ADULTS WOUNDED

A search of his St. Louis Park home turned up clothing matching what the shooter wore in surveillance video, according to the charges cited by FOX 9.

Police caught up with Adam Oct. 8 near Highway 55 and Penn Avenue in Minneapolis, taking him into custody without incident.

The Hennepin County Sheriff’s Office credited detectives with its Auto Theft Task Force and West Metro Drug Task Force, along with St. Louis Park and Hopkins officers, with safely boxing in the vehicle.

"I’m incredibly proud of our officers and investigators who have worked nonstop alongside our law enforcement partners to identify those responsible and hold them accountable," Eden Prairie Police Chief Matt Sackett said after the arrest.

AMY KLOBUCHAR CALLS FOR MAJOR ANTI-TERRORISM INVESTMENTS AFTER ALLEGED MALL OF AMERICA PLOT

The case has intensified concerns about Somali gang-related violence across the metro area, prompting regional public safety agencies to meet under the coordination of the Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension. Police leaders said they are sharing intelligence and coordinating investigations to prevent further shootings.

Republican U.S. Senate candidate Michele Tafoya pointed to the homecoming shooting and other recent violence while warning last week that Minnesotans increasingly feel under threat.

TRUMP’S LAW-AND-ORDER BLITZ MARKS ONE YEAR WITH EYE-POPPING HAUL OF SUSPECTS, GUNS IN BLUE CITY

"Our law enforcement here are calling it out as the product of Somali gang violence, and we’ve got to identify it, and we have to find a way to deal with it," Tafoya told Fox News Digital.

Eden Prairie police also are investigating an Oct. 5 shots-fired incident at a Speedway gas station, where no injuries were reported. Investigators said they have not identified a connection between that incident and the homecoming shooting.

Sackett said the homecoming investigation remains active, with additional arrests or charges possible.

Fox News Digital's Peter D'Abrosca contributed to this report.

item.title: Trump and Rubio weigh firing Kimberly Guilfoyle as misconduct and donor bailout allegations mount
item.description: Kimberly Guilfoyle faces mounting allegations in Greece as JD Vance and Marco Rubio weigh in on the embattled ambassador's growing controversies.
item.content:encoded:
U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle may soon be fired amid reports she sought a six-figure credit card bailout from a Trump donor while offering access to administration officials, adding to mounting allegations over her conduct in Athens.

President Donald Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio are "extremely pissed off" by Guilfoyle’s reported conduct and are weighing her removal, The Associated Press reported Sunday, citing a senior U.S. official.

The official told the AP that a decision on what action to take would likely come this week after Monday’s Columbus Day holiday. No departure has been confirmed.

Guilfoyle, onetime fiancée of Donald Trump Jr., came under scrutiny this week after The Wall Street Journal reported that she asked Trump donor Eric Deters to pay off a $100,000 American Express bill shortly before her Senate confirmation hearing.

MARCO RUBIO ANNOUNCES SWEEPING FINANCIAL SANCTIONS AGAINST THE INTERNATIONAL CRIMINAL COURT

According to messages reviewed by the Journal, Guilfoyle urged Deters to wire the money directly to American Express, saying the transaction would not leave a paper trail, while offering to help him gain access to senior Trump administration officials. Deters said he never made the payment.

Guilfoyle's attorney, Jesse Binnall, disputed the authenticity of the messages.

The allegations followed an earlier Journal investigation into Guilfoyle's conduct in Greece, including claims that she promoted the interests of Greek construction and energy company Aktor Group and allowed its registered lobbyist, Christos Marafatsos, to accompany her to private diplomatic meetings with senior officials.

FORMER TRUMP CABINET OFFICIAL HAD 'INAPPROPRIATELY CLOSE' RELATIONSHIP WITH BODYGUARD, IG FINDS

The Journal also reported that Guilfoyle suggested at a dinner with Greek officials that the U.S. would undermine their government, citing political developments in Romania. Greece's foreign minister has since said there was no need to summon Guilfoyle for an explanation because the country's energy minister denied that any threat had been made.

Separately, the State Department's Office of Inspector General opened an investigation into allegations involving Guilfoyle's treatment of embassy employees, private travel, acceptance of gifts and relationships with business interests, according to a report from the Daily Mail.

3 SECRET SERVICE OFFICIALS UNDER INTERNAL INVESTIGATION FOR POTENTIAL MISCONDUCT

Sources described a hostile workplace in which Guilfoyle allegedly threatened to fire employees. They also claim that she demoted members of her security detail over minor incidents, including an officer who reportedly failed to answer a 4 a.m. request for ice while she was vacationing in Mykonos.

The inspector general's office declined to confirm or deny the existence of an investigation. Binnall told the Daily Mail that "any implication of wrongdoing by the Ambassador is unsupported."

The allegations have drawn scrutiny from congressional Democrats, including Sen. Jeanne Shaheen, D-N.H., and Rep. Gregory Meeks, D-N.Y., who have called for a review of Guilfoyle's conduct. Meeks urged her removal if the allegations were substantiated.

Vice President JD Vance addressed the controversy Friday, cautioning against rushing to judgment while acknowledging that misconduct should carry consequences.

OHIO BAKERY WORKERS RECOUNT SURPRISE JD VANCE ENCOUNTER THAT TOOK AN UNEXPECTED TURN

"Let's actually see what the facts are. Let's see what the truth is," Vance told reporters in Ohio. "And obviously, if there was something bad that happened, then people have to suffer consequences for it."

Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who visited Greece this week and delivered remarks with the backdrop of Acropolis, declined to address the allegations directly.

SEC MARCO RUBIO: THE WEST FORGOT WHAT MADE IT GREAT. WE MUST REDISCOVER OUR ROOTS BEFORE WE LOSE THEM

"You guys walk around thinking that because some source told you something and you reported it, it's the gospel. It's not the gospel," Rubio told reporters Thursday.

Rubio had defended Guilfoyle's performance a day earlier, saying, "Our ambassador has been a strong ambassador here."

FOUR AMERICAN TOURISTS AMONG 6 KILLED AFTER EXPLOSION LEVELS BUILDING NEAR ATHENS’ ACROPOLIS

Trump nominated Guilfoyle to the diplomatic post in December 2024. A former California prosecutor and Fox News Channel personality, she previously served as a prominent surrogate and fundraiser for the president.

DONALD TRUMP JR AND BETTINA ANDERSON CELEBRATE PRIVATE WEDDING IN BAHAMAS, SHARE SWEET PERSONAL PHOTO

Guilfoyle was almost Trump’s daughter-in-law. She was engaged to Don Jr. for four years, but the two publicly split in Dec. 2024 — the same month the president nominated her to be the ambassador to Greece.

The president’s eldest son married Palm Beach socialite Bettina Anderson in May of this year.

She was also previously married to California Gov. Gavin Newsom, a Democrat, from 2001 to 2006, when he was serving as mayor of San Francisco.

item.title: Dre Greenlaw hits Sam Darnold along Seahawks bench, then chaos and ejection follow with more to come from NFL
item.description: Dre Greenlaw headbutted a helmetless Ernest Jones on the Seattle Seahawks sideline after hitting Sam Darnold out of bounds, leading to an ejection.
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw was ejected from Sunday's game against the Seattle Seahawks and could be subject to a suspension next week because he seemingly lost his poise and composure on the opponent's sideline and bench area.

Greenlaw hit Seattle's Sam Darnold as he was running out of bounds along the Seahawks sideline during the second quarter at Lumen Field. That got him flagged for a personal foul.

And because the play happened along the Seattle sideline and fully onto their bench area, Greenlaw was immediately surrounded by Seahawks players.

Seattle linebacker Ernest Jones, who has in the past offered a very moving verbal support for Darnold, got in Greenlaw's face.

The thing is, Greenlaw was wearing his helmet and Jones was not.

Greenlaw then headbutted Jones.

FOX NFL's cameras showed Jones using a towel to wipe his face, including an apparent cut caused by Greenlaw's headbutt.

NFL FINES SAINTS AND COWBOYS $500K FOR PRACTICE BRAWL, BUT FIGHTS WON'T STOP UNLESS PLAYERS GET FINED

Greenlaw was soon ejected from the game.

And what happens next will be up to the NFL, because there definitely will be more action from the league office.

FALCONS' JAMES PEARCE HIT WITH 8-GAME SUSPENSION AS NFL ANNOUNCES WAVE OF BANS ACROSS THE LEAGUE

According to NFL Operations guidelines, after the game, the NFL office reviews incidents such as this. The league can choose to issue a fine, a warning, or a suspension, depending on the severity of the action (such as throwing a punch or severe endangerment of an opponent).

Any suspension is a separate disciplinary ruling, not an automatic rule of disqualification.

KEENAN ALLEN FACES NFL SUSPENSION AFTER BLOOD ALCOHOL LEVEL NEARLY TRIPLE THE LEGAL LIMIT: REPORT

A suspension is only issued if the post-game review of the situation determines the act was "conduct detrimental to the League" or a severe violation of player safety.

This is decided on a case-by-case basis by the NFL’s disciplinary officers rather than as part of an automatic rule metric.

Greenlaw has a history of becoming emotional. And getting fined. And even suspended.

Following a 33-32 victory over the New York Giants in Week 7 of the 2025 season while playing for the Denver Broncos, Greenlaw chased and verbally threatened referee Brad Allen as the officiating crew was leaving the field.

NFL REFS HAVE SET ALL-TIME RECORD FOR FLAGS THIS SEASON, AND IT'S CHANGING THE OUTCOME OF GAMES

The league suspended Greenlaw, determining his aggressive post-game behavior violated Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1(b), which strictly prohibits the use of abusive, threatening, or insulting language or gestures toward game officials.

Last week, Greenlaw was fined $11,941 for unsportsmanlike conduct after taunting the Broncos' sideline and head coach Sean Payton.

A MASSIVE BRAWL AT COWBOYS AND SAINTS JOINT PRACTICE INCLUDES PUNCHES AND HELMETS THROWN AND WWE MOVES

And in 2023, Greenlaw was ejected following a sideline altercation with Philadelphia Eagles head of security Dom DiSandro during another incident along the opponent's sideline.

item.title: Commanders run out the clock on themselves, settle for tie with Giants in overtime meltdown
item.description: Jameis Winston rallied the Giants from 14 down, but a key fumble and Jayden Daniels' clock misread left both NFC East rivals stuck in a tie.
item.content:encoded:
The Giants and Commanders spent overtime trading ways to give the game away before settling for a tie.

The Giants and Commanders couldn’t settle Sunday’s back-and-forth game in regulation or overtime, finishing 27-27 for their second tie in three seasons.

Washington built a 14-point fourth-quarter lead before Jameis Winston rallied New York to force overtime. The real chaos was still to come.

GIANTS QUARTERBACK JAMEIS WINSTON CHANNELS HIS CHRISTIAN FAITH AFTER ANOTHER DRAMATIC VICTORY

The Giants appeared to have a chance to win with less than two minutes left in overtime. But as New York tried to run down the clock, Cam Skattebo fumbled, and Washington recovered.

The turnover gave the Commanders possession, but they still had work to do. They took over near midfield and needed a drive to get into field-goal range.

'I LOST US THAT GAME': NICK SIRIANNI MAKES DECISION THAT OPENED DOOR TO A JACKSONVILLE JAGUARS COMEBACK WIN

Washington answered with self-destruction.

Jayden Daniels, who ran for 103 yards, drove the Commanders to the Giants’ 24-yard line with 12 seconds remaining.

With no timeouts and facing second-and-8, Daniels scrambled for no gain. Washington couldn’t spike the ball before time expired, throwing away an easy shot for the game-winning boot.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Skattebo took responsibility for his fumble after the game. "At the end of the day I have to take care of the ball," he said. "I gotta hold on to the ball and make sure these guys know that when my name’s called, we’re gonna be okay."

As the game ended, coach Dan Quinn slammed his headset in frustration.

Quinn took responsibility for the final sequence after the game. "The sequencing of that does not fall on [Jayden]. ... I haven't spoken to him but that one's on me. We don't need to put him in that space." He summed up the result bluntly: "The tie feels like a loss."

NFL'S DUMBEST MOMENT OF WEEK 2 GOES TO JETS COACH AARON GLENN WHO PLAYED NOT TO LOSE AT END OF REGULATION

Daniels also accepted responsibility.

"We gotta relay that as a offense, it starts from everybody top down. Ultimately, it’s on me."

Commanders part-owner Magic Johnson offered his opinion on the game: "I’m in total disbelief my Commanders had such poor clock management in today’s overtime game against the Giants. All we had to do was kick the field goal and we would have won the game!"

No NFC East team won this week.

The Cowboys lost Thursday, and the Eagles fell earlier Sunday, but the Giants and Commanders couldn’t capitalize on the opening.

After 70 minutes, several missed field goals and two costly overtime mistakes, both teams walked away with a tie.
